source "https://rubygems.org"
git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

ruby "3.3.6"

# Bundle edge Rails instead: gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"
gem "rails", "7.0.8.7"
gem "concurrent-ruby", "1.3.4"

# The original asset pipeline for Rails [https://github.com/rails/sprockets-rails]
gem "sprockets-rails"

# Use postgresql as the database for Active Record
gem "pg", "1.6.0"

# Use the Puma web server [https://github.com/puma/puma]
gem "puma", "~> 5.0"

# Use JavaScript with ESM import maps [https://github.com/rails/importmap-rails]
gem "importmap-rails"

# Hotwire's SPA-like page accelerator [https://turbo.hotwired.dev]
gem "turbo-rails"

# Hotwire's modest JavaScript framework [https://stimulus.hotwired.dev]
gem "stimulus-rails"

# Build JSON APIs with ease [https://github.com/rails/jbuilder]
gem "jbuilder"

# Paginate the note list [https://github.com/ddnexus/pagy]
gem "pagy", "8.6.3"

# Run Active Job on Redis through Sidekiq [https://github.com/sidekiq/sidekiq]
gem "sidekiq", "6.5.12"
gem "redis", "4.8.1"

# Request citation metadata over HTTP [https://github.com/lostisland/faraday]
gem "faraday", "1.10.4"

# Use Kredis to get higher-level data types in Redis [https://github.com/rails/kredis]
# gem "kredis"

# Use Active Model has_secure_password [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_model_basics.html#securepassword]
gem "bcrypt", "~> 3.1.7"

# Windows does not include zoneinfo files, so bundle the tzinfo-data gem
gem "tzinfo-data", platforms: %i[ mingw mswin x64_mingw jruby ]

# Reduces boot times through caching; required in config/boot.rb
gem "bootsnap", require: false

# Use Sass to process CSS
# gem "sassc-rails"

# Use Active Storage variants [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_storage_overview.html#transforming-images]
# gem "image_processing", "~> 1.2"

group :development, :test do
  # See https://guides.rubyonrails.org/debugging_rails_applications.html#debugging-with-the-debug-gem
  gem "debug", platforms: %i[ mri mingw x64_mingw ]
end

group :development do
  # Use console on exceptions pages [https://github.com/rails/web-console]
  gem "web-console"

  # Add speed badges [https://github.com/MiniProfiler/rack-mini-profiler]
  # gem "rack-mini-profiler"

  # Speed up commands on slow machines / big apps [https://github.com/rails/spring]
  # gem "spring"
end

group :test do
  # Use system testing [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/testing.html#system-testing]
  gem "capybara"
  gem "selenium-webdriver"

  # Rails 7.0's test runner is incompatible with Minitest 6
  gem "minitest", "~> 5.25"
end

require_relative "boot"

require "rails/all"

# Require the gems listed in Gemfile, including any gems
# you've limited to :test, :development, or :production.
Bundler.require(*Rails.groups)

module MarginNotes
  class Application < Rails::Application
    # Initialize configuration defaults for originally generated Rails version.
    config.load_defaults 7.0

    # Configuration for the application, engines, and railties goes here.
    #
    # These settings can be overridden in specific environments using the files
    # in config/environments, which are processed later.
    #
    # config.time_zone = "Central Time (US & Canada)"
    # config.eager_load_paths << Rails.root.join("extras")

    # Jobs run in Sidekiq workers, which keep them in Redis (REDIS_URL, or
    # redis://localhost:6379 by default). Tests use Active Job's test adapter.
    config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq
  end
end
require "active_support/core_ext/integer/time"

Rails.application.configure do
  # Settings specified here will take precedence over those in config/application.rb.

  # In the development environment your application's code is reloaded any time
  # it changes. This slows down response time but is perfect for development
  # since you don't have to restart the web server when you make code changes.
  config.cache_classes = false

  # Do not eager load code on boot.
  config.eager_load = false

  # Show full error reports.
  config.consider_all_requests_local = true

  # Enable server timing
  config.server_timing = true

  # Enable/disable caching. By default caching is disabled.
  # Run rails dev:cache to toggle caching.
  if Rails.root.join("tmp/caching-dev.txt").exist?
    config.action_controller.perform_caching = true
    config.action_controller.enable_fragment_cache_logging = true

    config.cache_store = :memory_store
    config.public_file_server.headers = {
      "Cache-Control" => "public, max-age=#{2.days.to_i}"
    }
  else
    config.action_controller.perform_caching = false

    config.cache_store = :null_store
  end

  # Store uploaded files on the local file system (see config/storage.yml for options).
  config.active_storage.service = :local

  # Write email to files in tmp/mails, one per recipient, instead of sending it.
  config.action_mailer.delivery_method = :file
  config.action_mailer.file_settings = { location: Rails.root.join("tmp/mails") }
  config.action_mailer.raise_delivery_errors = true
  config.action_mailer.default_url_options = { host: "localhost", port: 3000 }

  config.action_mailer.perform_caching = false

  # Print deprecation notices to the Rails logger.
  config.active_support.deprecation = :log

  # Raise exceptions for disallowed deprecations.
  config.active_support.disallowed_deprecation = :raise

  # Tell Active Support which deprecation messages to disallow.
  config.active_support.disallowed_deprecation_warnings = []

  # Raise an error on page load if there are pending migrations.
  config.active_record.migration_error = :page_load

  # Highlight code that triggered database queries in logs.
  config.active_record.verbose_query_logs = true

  # Suppress logger output for asset requests.
  config.assets.quiet = true

  # Raises error for missing translations.
  # config.i18n.raise_on_missing_translations = true

  # Annotate rendered view with file names.
  # config.action_view.annotate_rendered_view_with_filenames = true

  # Uncomment if you wish to allow Action Cable access from any origin.
  # config.action_cable.disable_request_forgery_protection = true
end
require "active_support/core_ext/integer/time"

Rails.application.configure do
  # Settings specified here will take precedence over those in config/application.rb.

  # Code is not reloaded between requests.
  config.cache_classes = true

  # Eager load code on boot. This eager loads most of Rails and
  # your application in memory, allowing both threaded web servers
  # and those relying on copy on write to perform better.
  # Rake tasks automatically ignore this option for performance.
  config.eager_load = true

  # Full error reports are disabled and caching is turned on.
  config.consider_all_requests_local       = false
  config.action_controller.perform_caching = true

  # Ensures that a master key has been made available in either ENV["RAILS_MASTER_KEY"]
  # or in config/master.key. This key is used to decrypt credentials (and other encrypted files).
  # config.require_master_key = true

  # Disable serving static files from the `/public` folder by default since
  # Apache or NGINX already handles this.
  config.public_file_server.enabled = ENV["RAILS_SERVE_STATIC_FILES"].present?

  # Compress CSS using a preprocessor.
  # config.assets.css_compressor = :sass

  # Do not fallback to assets pipeline if a precompiled asset is missed.
  config.assets.compile = false

  # Enable serving of images, stylesheets, and JavaScripts from an asset server.
  # config.asset_host = "http://assets.example.com"

  # Specifies the header that your server uses for sending files.
  # config.action_dispatch.x_sendfile_header = "X-Sendfile" # for Apache
  # config.action_dispatch.x_sendfile_header = "X-Accel-Redirect" # for NGINX

  # Store uploaded files on the local file system (see config/storage.yml for options).
  config.active_storage.service = :local

  # Mount Action Cable outside main process or domain.
  # config.action_cable.mount_path = nil
  # config.action_cable.url = "wss://example.com/cable"
  # config.action_cable.allowed_request_origins = [ "http://example.com", /http:\/\/example.*/ ]

  # Force all access to the app over SSL, use Strict-Transport-Security, and use secure cookies.
  # config.force_ssl = true

  # Include generic and useful information about system operation, but avoid logging too much
  # information to avoid inadvertent exposure of personally identifiable information (PII).
  config.log_level = :info

  # Prepend all log lines with the following tags.
  config.log_tags = [ :request_id ]

  # Use a different cache store in production.
  # config.cache_store = :mem_cache_store

  # Use a real queuing backend for Active Job (and separate queues per environment).
  # config.active_job.queue_adapter     = :resque
  # config.active_job.queue_name_prefix = "margin_notes_production"

  config.action_mailer.perform_caching = false

  # Ignore bad email addresses and do not raise email delivery errors.

  # config.action_mailer.raise_delivery_errors = false

  # Enable locale fallbacks for I18n (makes lookups for any locale fall back to
  # the I18n.default_locale when a translation cannot be found).
  config.i18n.fallbacks = true

  # Don't log any deprecations.
  config.active_support.report_deprecations = false

  # Use default logging formatter so that PID and timestamp are not suppressed.
  config.log_formatter = ::Logger::Formatter.new

  # Use a different logger for distributed setups.
  # require "syslog/logger"
  # config.logger = ActiveSupport::TaggedLogging.new(Syslog::Logger.new "app-name")

  if ENV["RAILS_LOG_TO_STDOUT"].present?
    logger           = ActiveSupport::Logger.new(STDOUT)
    logger.formatter = config.log_formatter
    config.logger    = ActiveSupport::TaggedLogging.new(logger)
  end

  # Do not dump schema after migrations.
  config.active_record.dump_schema_after_migration = false
end
require "active_support/core_ext/integer/time"

# The test environment is used exclusively to run your application's
# test suite. You never need to work with it otherwise. Remember that
# your test database is "scratch space" for the test suite and is wiped
# and recreated between test runs. Don't rely on the data there!

Rails.application.configure do
  # Settings specified here will take precedence over those in config/application.rb.

  # Turn false under Spring and add config.action_view.cache_template_loading = true.
  config.cache_classes = true

  # Eager loading loads your whole application. When running a single test locally,

  config.eager_load = ENV["CI"].present?

  # Configure public file server for tests with Cache-Control for performance.
  config.public_file_server.enabled = true
  config.public_file_server.headers = {
    "Cache-Control" => "public, max-age=#{1.hour.to_i}"
  }

  # Show full error reports and disable caching.
  config.consider_all_requests_local       = true
  config.action_controller.perform_caching = false
  config.cache_store = :null_store

  # Raise exceptions instead of rendering exception templates.
  config.action_dispatch.show_exceptions = false

  # Disable request forgery protection in test environment.
  config.action_controller.allow_forgery_protection = false

  # Queue jobs in memory. Tests perform them explicitly.
  config.active_job.queue_adapter = :test

  # Store uploaded files on the local file system in a temporary directory.
  config.active_storage.service = :test

  config.action_mailer.perform_caching = false

  # Tell Action Mailer not to deliver emails to the real world.
  # The :test delivery method accumulates sent emails in the
  # ActionMailer::Base.deliveries array.
  config.action_mailer.delivery_method = :test
  config.action_mailer.default_url_options = { host: "www.example.com" }

  # Print deprecation notices to the stderr.
  config.active_support.deprecation = :stderr

  # Raise exceptions for disallowed deprecations.
  config.active_support.disallowed_deprecation = :raise

  # Tell Active Support which deprecation messages to disallow.
  config.active_support.disallowed_deprecation_warnings = []

  # Raises error for missing translations.
  # config.i18n.raise_on_missing_translations = true

  # Annotate rendered view with file names.
  # config.action_view.annotate_rendered_view_with_filenames = true
end
# PostgreSQL. Versions 9.3 and up are supported.
#
# Install the pg driver:
#   gem install pg
# On macOS with Homebrew:
#   gem install pg -- --with-pg-config=/usr/local/bin/pg_config
# On macOS with MacPorts:
#   gem install pg -- --with-pg-config=/opt/local/lib/postgresql84/bin/pg_config
# On Windows:

  adapter: postgresql
  encoding: unicode
  # For details on connection pooling, see Rails configuration guide

class ApplicationRecord < ActiveRecord::Base
  primary_abstract_class
end
# A work identified by its DOI, shared by every reader who cites it. Readers'
# own annotations stay on their notes. Its metadata, and the state of the latest
# request for it, are shared too.
class Citation < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :notes, foreign_key: :citation_doi

  enum :enrichment_status, { pending: 0, completed: 1, failed: 2 }, prefix: :enrichment

  validates :doi, format: { with: %r{\A10\.\d{4,9}/\S+\z} }

  # Marks the citation pending and queues a metadata lookup, unless one is
  # already pending. Returns whether a lookup was queued. The job is queued under
  # the row lock, so a failed enqueue rolls back the pending state.
  def request_enrichment
    with_lock do
      if enrichment_pending?
        false
      else
        update!(enrichment_status: :pending, enrichment_error: nil)
        CitationEnrichmentJob.perform_later(self)
        true
      end
    end
  end

  # Asks the provider for this DOI's metadata. A permanent refusal marks the
  # enrichment failed; an unavailable provider raises so the job can retry.
  def enrich
    metadata = Provider.new.lookup(doi)
    record_enrichment(title: metadata.title, source_url: metadata.source_url, enrichment_status: :completed, enrichment_error: nil)
  rescue Provider::Error => error
    fail_enrichment(error.message)
  end

  def fail_enrichment(reason)
    record_enrichment(enrichment_status: :failed, enrichment_error: reason)
  end

  private
    # The job can load this citation before the request that queued it commits.
    # Taking the row lock waits for that commit and reloads, so the result is
    # written even when it equals the values loaded earlier.
    def record_enrichment(attributes)
      with_lock { update!(attributes) }
    end
end
# A Markdown file of one notebook's notes, written by ExportJob. The reader can
# cancel it while it is queued or working; the worker checks between notes and
# stops. A completed file can be downloaded until it expires.
class Export < ApplicationRecord
  AVAILABLE_FOR = 24.hours

  belongs_to :notebook
  has_one_attached :file

  enum :status, { queued: 0, working: 1, completed: 2, cancelled: 3 }

  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  def cancellable?
    queued? || working?
  end

  # Cancels a queued or working export. Returns whether it was cancelled.
  def cancel
    with_lock do
      if cancellable?
        update!(status: :cancelled)
      else
        false
      end
    end
  end

  # Writes the notebook's notes, oldest first, under its export heading. Progress
  # is saved after each note. A cancelled export stops before the next note and
  # keeps no file.
  def generate
    notes = notebook.notes.with_rich_text_body.order(:created_at, :id).to_a
    return unless start(notes.size)

    fragments = ["# #{notebook.export_heading || notebook.name}\n"]
    notes.each_with_index do |note, index|
      fragments << markdown_for(note)
      return unless record_progress(index + 1)
    end

    finish(fragments.sum)
  end

  # The authoritative check for downloading the file.
  def downloadable?
    completed? && expires_at.future?
  end

  private
    # A retried job starts again from the first note.
    def start(total)
      with_lock do
        update!(status: :working, processed_notes_count: 0, total_notes_count: total) if cancellable?
      end
    end

    def record_progress(count)
      with_lock do
        update!(processed_notes_count: count) unless cancelled?
      end
    end

    # The file is stored before the export is marked completed, so a completed
    # export always has one.
    def finish(markdown)
      blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(io: StringIO.new(markdown),
        filename: "#{notebook.slug}.md", content_type: "text/markdown")

      completed = with_lock do
        update!(file: blob, status: :completed, expires_at: AVAILABLE_FOR.from_now) unless cancelled?
      end

      blob.purge unless completed
    end

    def markdown_for(note)
      body = note.body.to_plain_text.strip
      markdown = "\n## #{note.title.squish}\n"
      markdown += "\n#{body}\n" if body.present?
      markdown
    end
end
require "csv"

# A CSV of notes for one notebook. A preview reads and validates the rows without
# saving anything. Applying validates them again and saves the import with every
# row's note, or saves nothing.
class Import < ApplicationRecord
  HEADERS = %w[ title body_html doi annotation reminder_epoch ]
  MAXIMUM_SIZE = 100.kilobytes
  MAXIMUM_ROWS = 100

  Row = Struct.new(:line, :note, :annotation)

  belongs_to :notebook
  has_many :notes, dependent: :nullify

  validate :csv_is_importable, on: :create

  # Reads one byte past the limit, which is enough to reject a larger file.
  def file=(upload)
    self.csv = String.new(upload.read(MAXIMUM_SIZE + 1).to_s, encoding: Encoding::UTF_8)
  end

  def csv
    @csv.to_s
  end

  def csv=(text)
    @csv = text.to_s
    @rows = nil
  end

  def rows
    parse unless @rows
    @rows
  end

  # The reader's annotations by source line.
  def annotations
    rows.each_with_object(ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess.new) do |row, annotations|
      annotations[row.line] = row.annotation
    end
  end

  # Validates the file and every row without saving. Returns whether the import
  # can be applied, leaving the errors on the import and each row's note.
  def preview
    valid? && rows.map { |row| row.note.valid? }.all?
  end

  def apply
    return false if invalid?

    transaction do
      save!
      rows.each do |row|
        return false unless row.note.save
      end
    end

    true
  end

  def receipt
    CSV.generate do |csv|
      csv << %w[ title doi ]
      notes.includes(:citation).order(:id).each do |note|
        citation = note.citation
        csv << [ note.title, citation && citation[:id] ]
      end
    end
  end

  private
    def parse
      @rows, @headers, @problem = [], nil, nil
      return if csv.bytesize > MAXIMUM_SIZE || !csv.valid_encoding?

      reader = CSV.new(csv.delete_prefix("\uFEFF").encode(universal_newline: true))
      citations = {}
      next_line = 1

      reader.each do |fields|
        line, next_line = next_line, next_line + reader.line.count("\n")

        if @headers.nil?
          @headers = fields.map { |field| field.to_s.strip }
          break if @headers != HEADERS
        elsif fields.size != HEADERS.size && fields.any?
          @problem = "line #{line} has #{fields.size} fields instead of #{HEADERS.size}"
          break
        elsif fields.any?
          @rows << build_row(line, fields, citations)
          break if @rows.size > MAXIMUM_ROWS
        end
      end
    rescue CSV::MalformedCSVError => error
      @problem = "it is not valid CSV (#{error.message})"
    end

    # Rows naming the same DOI share one citation, so it is created only once.
    def build_row(line, fields, citations)
      title, body_html, doi, annotation, reminder_epoch = fields.map { |field| field.to_s.strip }
      citation = citations[doi] ||= Citation.find_or_initialize_by(doi: doi) if doi.present?

      note = Note.new(notebook: notebook, import: self, title: title, body: body_html, citation: citation,
        annotation: annotation.presence, reminder_epoch: reminder_epoch.presence)

      Row.new(line, note, annotation.presence)
    end

    def csv_is_importable
      rows

      if csv.empty?
        errors.add(:csv, :blank)
      elsif csv.bytesize > MAXIMUM_SIZE
        errors.add(:csv, "must be #{ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(MAXIMUM_SIZE)} or smaller")
      elsif !csv.valid_encoding?
        errors.add(:csv, "must be UTF-8 text")
      elsif @problem
        errors.add(:csv, "cannot be read because #{@problem}")
      elsif @headers != HEADERS
        errors.add(:csv, "must start with the header row #{HEADERS.join(",")}")
      elsif rows.empty?
        errors.add(:csv, "must contain at least one note")
      elsif rows.size > MAXIMUM_ROWS
        errors.add(:csv, "must contain #{MAXIMUM_ROWS} notes or fewer")
      end
    end
end
class Note < ApplicationRecord
  HIGHLIGHT_COLORS = %w[ yellow green blue pink ]
  MAXIMUM_ATTACHMENT_SIZE = 1.megabyte

  belongs_to :notebook
  belongs_to :import, optional: true
  belongs_to :citation, optional: true, foreign_key: :citation_doi, validate: true
  has_rich_text :body

  enum status: { draft: 0, ready: 1 }, _prefix: true

  serialize :tags, JSON
  store_accessor :settings, :color
  alias_attribute :highlight_color, :color

  validates :title, presence: true
  validates :color, inclusion: { in: HIGHLIGHT_COLORS }, allow_blank: true
  validates :reminder_epoch, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than: 0, less_than: 10_000_000_000 }, allow_nil: true
  validate :attachments_are_small

  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :titled_like, ->(query) { where("notes.title ILIKE ?", "%#{sanitize_sql_like(query)}%") }

  def doi
    citation_doi
  end

  # Cites the shared citation with this exact DOI, ignoring surrounding whitespace.
  # A blank DOI removes the citation from the note.
  def doi=(doi)
    doi = doi.to_s.strip
    self.citation = (Citation.find_or_initialize_by(doi: doi) if doi.present?)
  end

  # The reminder time in the reader's time zone.
  def reminder_at
    Time.find_zone!(notebook.user.time_zone).at(reminder_epoch) if reminder_epoch
  end

  # Twenty-four elapsed hours after the reminder time, for postponing it a day.
  # The result keeps the reminder's UTC offset, so across a daylight saving
  # change its wall-clock time differs from the reader's local time.
  def next_day_reminder_at
    reminder_at.to_time + 86_400
  end

  def reminder_scheduled?
    reminder_job_id.present? && reminder_sent_at.nil?
  end

  # Schedules an email reminder at the given time in seconds since 1970, by
  # default the stored one, such as an imported reminder. It replaces any
  # earlier reminder for this note: the earlier job sends nothing when it runs.
  # Returns whether the reminder was scheduled. The job is queued under the row
  # lock, so a failed enqueue leaves the previous reminder in place.
  def schedule_reminder(epoch = reminder_epoch)
    with_lock do
      self.reminder_epoch = epoch

      if reminder_epoch && valid?
        job = NoteReminderJob.set(wait_until: reminder_epoch).perform_later(self)
        update!(reminder_job_id: job.job_id, reminder_sent_at: nil)
      else
        errors.add(:base, "Choose a date and time for the reminder") if reminder_epoch.nil?
        restore_attributes([:reminder_epoch])
        false
      end
    end
  end

  def postpone_reminder
    reminder_scheduled? && schedule_reminder(next_day_reminder_at.to_i)
  end

  # Sends the reminder if the given job is still the one scheduled for it.
  # Taking the row lock waits for the request that queued the job to commit.
  def send_reminder(job_id)
    with_lock do
      if reminder_job_id == job_id && reminder_scheduled?
        update!(reminder_sent_at: Time.current)
        ReminderMailer.with(note: self).note_reminder.deliver_now
      end
    end
  end

  def tag_list
    tags.join(", ")
  end

  def tag_list=(list)
    self.tags = list.to_s.split(",").map(&:strip).reject(&:blank?).uniq
  end

  private
    def attachments_are_small
      if body.body&.attachables.to_a.grep(ActiveStorage::Blob).any? { |blob| blob.byte_size > MAXIMUM_ATTACHMENT_SIZE }
        errors.add(:body, "attachments must be #{ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(MAXIMUM_ATTACHMENT_SIZE)} or smaller")
      end
    end
end
class Notebook < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :user
  has_many :notes, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :imports, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :exports, dependent: :destroy

  serialize :preferences
  attr_readonly :slug

  before_validation :assign_slug, on: :create

  validates :name, presence: true

  def export_heading
    preferences.to_h["export_heading"]
  end

  def export_heading=(heading)
    self.preferences = preferences.to_h.merge("export_heading" => heading.to_s.strip.presence).compact
  end

  # Queues a Markdown export. The export is saved before its job is queued, so
  # the worker can always load it, and removed again if Redis refuses the job.
  def request_export
    export = exports.create!
    export.update!(job_id: ExportJob.perform_async(export.id, { format: "markdown" }))
    export
  rescue Redis::BaseError
    export&.destroy
    raise
  end

  # The number of notes, in any status, created on each UTC date, newest date
  # first, as [date, count] pairs. Dates without notes are omitted. Only notes
  # that still exist are counted, so deleting a note lowers its date's count.
  # Timestamps are stored in UTC, so their date part is the UTC date. The raw
  # select returns that date as PostgreSQL's ISO 8601 text.
  def daily_note_counts
    days = notes.select("DATE(notes.created_at) AS day, COUNT(*) AS notes_count").group("day").order("day DESC")
    Note.connection.select_rows(days).map { |day, count| [Date.iso8601(day), count] }
  end

  private
    def assign_slug
      self.slug = name.to_s.parameterize.presence || "notebook"
    end
end
class User < ApplicationRecord
  # Keep digest reservations past the end of their UTC day.
  DIGEST_RESERVATIONS_KEPT_FOR = 2.days

  has_secure_password

  has_many :notebooks, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :notes, through: :notebooks

  before_validation { self.email = email.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :email, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :time_zone, inclusion: { in: ActiveSupport::TimeZone.all.map(&:name) }

  def self.authenticate(email, password)
    find_by(email: email.to_s.strip.downcase)&.authenticate(password)
  end

  # Reads a date and time the reader entered, such as "2026-10-31T09:00", in
  # their time zone. Returns nil when it is blank or not a valid time.
  def local_time(text)
    Time.find_zone!(time_zone).iso8601(text.to_s) if text.present?
  rescue ArgumentError
    nil
  end

  # Queues an email digest of ready notes updated today (UTC), unless the reader
  # has already requested one for that UTC day. Returns whether a digest was queued.
  #
  # A Redis set of reader IDs for each day holds the reservations. If the job
  # cannot be queued, the reservation is released and the error raised, so the
  # reader can ask again. This prevents repeated requests, not repeated
  # deliveries: a job that Sidekiq retries can send its digest more than once.
  def request_digest
    requested_at = Time.current.in_time_zone(time_zone)
    key = "digest_requests:#{requested_at.utc.to_date.iso8601}"

    if Sidekiq.redis { |redis| redis.sadd(key, id) }
      begin
        Sidekiq.redis { |redis| redis.expire(key, DIGEST_RESERVATIONS_KEPT_FOR.to_i) }
        DigestJob.perform_later(self, requested_at, reading_completion)
      rescue StandardError
        Sidekiq.redis { |redis| redis.srem(key, id) }
        raise
      end

      true
    else
      false
    end
  end

  # The share of the reader's notes that are ready, from 0 to 1.
  def reading_completion
    total = notes.count
    total.zero? ? BigDecimal("0") : (BigDecimal(notes.status_ready.count) / total).round(4)
  end
end
# The configured citation metadata service. It answers GET /works?doi=... with a
# JSON title and source URL, using HTTP basic authentication. Settings come from
# config/secrets.yml, which reads them from the environment.
class Citation::Provider
  # The provider answered, but cannot supply metadata for this DOI.
  class Error < StandardError; end

  # The provider cannot answer now. Asking again later may succeed.
  class Unavailable < StandardError; end

  Metadata = Struct.new(:title, :source_url)

  def initialize(settings = Rails.application.secrets.citation_provider.to_h)
    @url, @user, @password = settings.values_at(:url, :user, :password)
  end

  def lookup(doi)
    raise Error, "No citation provider is configured" if @url.blank?

    response = connection.get("works", doi: doi)

    case response.status
    when 200 then metadata_from(response.body)
    when 401, 403 then raise Error, "The provider rejected the configured credentials (HTTP #{response.status})"
    when 404 then raise Error, "The provider has no record of this DOI"
    when 429, 500..599 then raise Unavailable, "The provider is unavailable (HTTP #{response.status})"
    else raise Error, "The provider gave an unexpected response (HTTP #{response.status})"
    end
  rescue Faraday::ConnectionFailed, Faraday::TimeoutError => error
    raise Unavailable, "The provider could not be reached (#{error.message})"
  end

  private
    # Retries a GET once on 503 before reporting the provider unavailable.
    def connection
      Faraday.new(url: @url, request: { open_timeout: 2, timeout: 5 }) do |faraday|
        faraday.request :retry, max: 1, retry_statuses: [503]
        faraday.request :basic_auth, @user, @password
      end
    end

    def metadata_from(body)
      attributes = JSON.parse(body)
      title, source_url = attributes["title"], attributes["url"] if attributes.is_a?(Hash)

      if title.is_a?(String) && title.present? && web_url?(source_url)
        Metadata.new(title.strip, source_url)
      else
        raise Error, "The provider's response did not include a title and web address"
      end
    rescue JSON::ParserError
      raise Error, "The provider's response was not valid JSON"
    end

    def web_url?(url)
      uri = URI.parse(url.to_s)
      uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) && uri.host.present?
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      false
    end
end
class ApplicationJob < ActiveJob::Base
  # Automatically retry jobs that encountered a deadlock
  # retry_on ActiveRecord::Deadlocked

  # Most jobs are safe to ignore if the underlying records are no longer available
  # discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError
end
class CitationEnrichmentJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :default

  # Three attempts in all, each of which may already have retried once on 503.
  # After the last, the failure is recorded rather than handed to the queue's
  # own retries.
  retry_on Citation::Provider::Unavailable, wait: :exponentially_longer, attempts: 3 do |job, error|
    job.arguments.first.fail_enrichment(error.message)
  end

  def perform(citation)
    citation.enrich
  end
end
class DigestJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :default

  # The request time arrives in the worker's time zone, and the completion as
  # the decimal string it was stored as in the queue. See User#request_digest.
  def perform(reader, requested_at, completion)
    DigestMailer.with(reader: reader, requested_at: requested_at, completion: completion).daily_digest.deliver_now
  end
end
# A native Sidekiq job, so its job ID can be shown with the export. Sidekiq
# stores arguments as JSON, so the options arrive with string keys.
class ExportJob
  include Sidekiq::Job

  def perform(export_id, options)
    format = options.fetch("format")
    raise ArgumentError, "Unsupported export format: #{format}" unless format == "markdown"

    Export.find(export_id).generate
  end
end
class NoteReminderJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :default

  # The note may have been deleted while its reminder was scheduled.
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  def perform(note)
    note.send_reminder(job_id)
  end
end
class ApplicationMailer < ActionMailer::Base
  default from: "from@example.com"
  layout "mailer"
end
class DigestMailer < ApplicationMailer
  # Lists the reader's ready notes last updated on the day of the request.
  # Active Job deserializes the request time in the worker's time zone (UTC),
  # so that is the day the digest covers, which can differ from the reader's
  # local day near midnight.
  def daily_digest
    @reader, requested_at = params.values_at(:reader, :requested_at)
    @date = requested_at.to_date
    @notes = @reader.notes.status_ready.where(updated_at: requested_at.all_day).includes(:notebook).order(:updated_at, :id)
    @completion = BigDecimal(params[:completion])

    mail to: @reader.email, subject: "Your reading digest for #{l @date, format: :long}"
  end
end
class ReminderMailer < ApplicationMailer
  def note_reminder
    @note = params[:note]
    mail to: @note.notebook.user.email, subject: "Reminder: #{@note.title}"
  end
end

module ActiveJob
  module Serializers
    class TimeWithZoneSerializer < ObjectSerializer # :nodoc:
      NANO_PRECISION = 9

      def serialize(time_with_zone)
        super(
          "value" => time_with_zone.iso8601(NANO_PRECISION),
          "time_zone" => time_with_zone.time_zone.tzinfo.name
        )
      end

      def deserialize(hash)
        Time.iso8601(hash["value"]).in_time_zone(hash["time_zone"] || Time.zone)
      end

      def klass
        ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone
      end
    end
  end

        if argument.class == String
          argument
        else
          begin
            Serializers.serialize(argument)
          rescue SerializationError
            argument
          end
        end
      when Symbol
        { OBJECT_SERIALIZER_KEY => "ActiveJob::Serializers::SymbolSerializer", "value" => argument.name }
      when GlobalID::Identification
        convert_to_global_id_hash(argument)
      when Array
        argument.map { |arg| serialize_argument(arg) }
      when ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess
        serialize_indifferent_hash(argument)
      when Hash
        symbol_keys = argument.keys
        symbol_keys.select! { |k| k.is_a?(Symbol) }
        symbol_keys.map!(&:name)

        aj_hash_key = if Hash.ruby2_keywords_hash?(argument)
          RUBY2_KEYWORDS_KEY
        else
          SYMBOL_KEYS_KEY
        end
        result = serialize_hash(argument)
        result[aj_hash_key] = symbol_keys
        result
      else
        Serializers.serialize(argument)
      end
    end

    # Deserializes a set of arguments. Intrinsic types that can safely be
    # deserialized without mutation are returned as-is. Arrays/Hashes are
    # deserialized element by element. All other types are deserialized using
    # GlobalID.
    def deserialize(arguments)
      arguments.map { |argument| deserialize_argument(argument) }
    rescue
      raise DeserializationError
    end

    private
      # :nodoc:
      GLOBALID_KEY = "_aj_globalid"
      # :nodoc:
      SYMBOL_KEYS_KEY = "_aj_symbol_keys"
      # :nodoc:
      RUBY2_KEYWORDS_KEY = "_aj_ruby2_keywords"
      # :nodoc:
      WITH_INDIFFERENT_ACCESS_KEY = "_aj_hash_with_indifferent_access"
      # :nodoc:
      OBJECT_SERIALIZER_KEY = "_aj_serialized"

      # :nodoc:
      RESERVED_KEYS = [
        GLOBALID_KEY, GLOBALID_KEY.to_sym,
        SYMBOL_KEYS_KEY, SYMBOL_KEYS_KEY.to_sym,
        RUBY2_KEYWORDS_KEY, RUBY2_KEYWORDS_KEY.to_sym,
        OBJECT_SERIALIZER_KEY, OBJECT_SERIALIZER_KEY.to_sym,
        WITH_INDIFFERENT_ACCESS_KEY, WITH_INDIFFERENT_ACCESS_KEY.to_sym,
      ].to_set
      private_constant :RESERVED_KEYS, :GLOBALID_KEY,
        :SYMBOL_KEYS_KEY, :RUBY2_KEYWORDS_KEY, :WITH_INDIFFERENT_ACCESS_KEY

      def deserialize_argument(argument)
        case argument
        when nil, true, false, String, Integer, Float
          argument
        when Array
          argument.map { |arg| deserialize_argument(arg) }
        when Hash
          if serialized_global_id?(argument)
            deserialize_global_id argument
          elsif custom_serialized?(argument)
            Serializers.deserialize(argument)
          else
            deserialize_hash(argument)
          end
        else
          raise ArgumentError, "Can only deserialize primitive arguments: #{argument.inspect}"
        end
      end

      def serialized_global_id?(hash)
        hash.size == 1 && hash.include?(GLOBALID_KEY)
      end

      def deserialize_global_id(hash)
        GlobalID::Locator.locate hash[GLOBALID_KEY]
      end

      def custom_serialized?(hash)
        hash.key?(OBJECT_SERIALIZER_KEY)
      end

## Rails 7.1.0.rc1 (September 27, 2023) ##

*   Set `scheduled_at` attribute as a Time object instead of epoch seconds, and serialize and deserialize the value
    when enqueued. Assigning a numeric/epoch value to scheduled_at= is deprecated; use a Time object instead.

    Deserializes `enqueued_at` as a Time instead of ISO8601 String.

    *Ben Sheldon*

*   Clarify the backoff strategy for the recommended `:wait` option when retrying jobs

    `wait: :exponentially_longer` is waiting polynomially longer, so it is now recommended to use `wait: :polynomially_longer` to keep the same behavior.

## Rails 7.1.0.beta1 (September 13, 2023) ##

*   Fix Active Job log message to correctly report a job failed to enqueue
    when the adapter raises an `ActiveJob::EnqueueError`.

    *Ben Sheldon*

*   Add `after_discard` method.

    This method lets job authors define a block which will be run when a job is about to be discarded. For example:

    ```ruby
    class AfterDiscardJob < ActiveJob::Base
      after_discard do |job, exception|
        Rails.logger.info("#{job.class} raised an exception: #{exception}")
      end

      def perform
        raise StandardError
      end
    end
    ```

    The above job will run the block passed to `after_discard` after the job is discarded. The exception will
    still be raised after the block has been run.

    *Rob Cardy*

*   Fix deserialization of ActiveSupport::Duration

    Previously, a deserialized Duration would return an array from Duration#parts.
    It will now return a hash just like a regular Duration.

    This also fixes an error when trying to add or subtract from a deserialized Duration
    (eg `duration + 1.year`).

    *Jonathan del Strother*

*   `perform_enqueued_jobs` is now compatible with all Active Job adapters

    This means that methods that depend on it, like Action Mailer's `assert_emails`,
    will work correctly even if the test adapter is not used.

    *Alex Ghiculescu*

*   Allow queue adapters to provide a custom name by implementing `queue_adapter_name`

    *Sander Verdonschot*

*   Log background job enqueue callers

    Add `verbose_enqueue_logs` configuration option to display the caller
    of background job enqueue in the log to help with debugging.

    Example log line:

    ```
    Enqueued AvatarThumbnailsJob (Job ID: ab528951-41fb-4c48-9129-3171791c27d6) to Sidekiq(default) with arguments: 1092412064
    ↳ app/models/user.rb:421:in `generate_avatar_thumbnails'
    ```

    Enabled in development only for new and upgraded applications. Not recommended for use
    in the production environment since it relies on Ruby's `Kernel#caller` which is fairly slow.

    *fatkodima*

*   Set `provider_job_id` for Backburner jobs

    *Cameron Matheson*

*   Add `perform_all_later` to enqueue multiple jobs at once

    This adds the ability to bulk enqueue jobs, without running callbacks, by
    passing multiple jobs or an array of jobs. For example:

    ```ruby
    ActiveJob.perform_all_later(MyJob.new("hello", 42), MyJob.new("world", 0))

    user_jobs = User.pluck(:id).map { |id| UserJob.new(user_id: id) }
    ActiveJob.perform_all_later(user_jobs)
    ```

    This can greatly reduce the number of round-trips to the queue datastore.
    For queue adapters that do not implement the new `enqueue_all` method, we
    fall back to enqueuing jobs individually. The Sidekiq adapter implements
    `enqueue_all` with `push_bulk`.

    This method does not use the existing `enqueue.active_job` event, but adds a
    new event `enqueue_all.active_job`.

    *Sander Verdonschot*

*   Don't double log the `job` when using `ActiveRecord::QueryLog`

    Previously if you set `config.active_record.query_log_tags` to an array that included
    `:job`, the job name would get logged twice. This bug has been fixed.

    *Alex Ghiculescu*

*   Add support for Sidekiq's transaction-aware client

    *Jonathan del Strother*

*   Remove QueAdapter from Active Job.

    After maintaining Active Job QueAdapter by Rails and Que side
    to support Ruby 3 keyword arguments and options provided as top level keywords,
    it is quite difficult to maintain it this way.

    Active Job Que adapter can be included in the future version of que gem itself.

    *Yasuo Honda*

*   Fix BigDecimal (de)serialization for adapters using JSON.

    Previously, BigDecimal was listed as not needing a serializer.  However,
    when used with an adapter storing the job arguments as JSON, it would get
    serialized as a simple String, resulting in deserialization also producing
    a String (instead of a BigDecimal).

    By using a serializer, we ensure the round trip is safe.

    To ensure applications using BigDecimal job arguments are not subject to
    race conditions during deployment (where a replica running a version of
    Rails without BigDecimalSerializer fails to deserialize an argument
    serialized with it), `ActiveJob.use_big_decimal_serializer` is disabled by
    default, and can be set to true in a following deployment..

    *Sam Bostock*

*   Preserve full-precision `enqueued_at` timestamps for serialized jobs,
    allowing more accurate reporting of how long a job spent waiting in the
    queue before it was performed.

    Retains IS08601 format compatibility.

    *Jeremy Daer*

*   Add `--parent` option to job generator to specify parent class of job.

    Example:

    `bin/rails g job process_payment --parent=payment_job` generates:

    ```ruby
    class ProcessPaymentJob < PaymentJob
      # ...
    end
    ```

    *Gannon McGibbon*

*   Add more detailed description to job generator.

    *Gannon McGibbon*

*   `perform.active_job` notification payloads now include `:db_runtime`, which
    is the total time (in ms) taken by database queries while performing a job.
    This value can be used to better understand how a job's time is spent.

    *Jonathan Hefner*

*   Update `ActiveJob::QueueAdapters::QueAdapter` to remove deprecation warning.

    Remove a deprecation warning introduced in que 1.2 to prepare for changes in
    que 2.0 necessary for Ruby 3 compatibility.

    *Damir Zekic* and *Adis Hasovic*

*   Add missing `bigdecimal` require in `ActiveJob::Arguments`

    Could cause `uninitialized constant ActiveJob::Arguments::BigDecimal (NameError)`
    when loading Active Job in isolation.

    *Jean Boussier*

*   Allow testing `discard_on/retry_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError`

    Previously in `perform_enqueued_jobs`, `deserialize_arguments_if_needed`
    was called before calling `perform_now`. When a record no longer exists
    and is serialized using GlobalID this led to raising
    an `ActiveJob::DeserializationError` before reaching `perform_now` call.
    This behavior makes difficult testing the job `discard_on/retry_on` logic.

    Now `deserialize_arguments_if_needed` call is postponed to when `perform_now`
    is called.

    Example:

    ```ruby
    class UpdateUserJob < ActiveJob::Base
      discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

      def perform(user)
        # ...
      end
    end

    # In the test
    User.destroy_all
    assert_nothing_raised do
      perform_enqueued_jobs only: UpdateUserJob
    end
    ```

    *Jacopo Beschi*

*   All tests now respect the `active_job.queue_adapter` config.

*   Make Active Job transaction aware when used conjointly with Active Record.

    A common mistake with Active Job is to enqueue jobs from inside a transaction,
    causing them to potentially be picked and ran by another process, before the
    transaction is committed, which may result in various errors.

    ```ruby
    Topic.transaction do
      topic = Topic.create(...)
      NewTopicNotificationJob.perform_later(topic)
    end
    ```

    Now Active Job will automatically defer the enqueuing to after the transaction is committed,
    and drop the job if the transaction is rolled back.

    Various queue implementations can choose to disable this behavior, and users can disable it,
    or force it on a per job basis:

    ```ruby
    class NewTopicNotificationJob < ApplicationJob
      self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = :never # or `:always` or `:default`
    end
    ```

      def determine_delay(seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm:, executions:, jitter: JITTER_DEFAULT)
        jitter = jitter == JITTER_DEFAULT ? self.class.retry_jitter : (jitter || 0.0)

        case seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm

        when ActiveSupport::Duration, Integer

class Range # :nodoc:
  # Optimize range sum to use arithmetic progression if a block is not given and
  # we have a range of numeric values.
  def sum(initial_value = 0)
    if block_given? || !(first.is_a?(Integer) && last.is_a?(Integer))
      super
    else
      actual_last = exclude_end? ? (last - 1) : last
      if actual_last >= first
        sum = initial_value || 0
        sum + (actual_last - first + 1) * (actual_last + first) / 2
      else
        initial_value || 0
      end
    end
  end

require "rails-html-sanitizer"

module ActionText
  module ContentHelper
    mattr_accessor(:sanitizer, default: Rails::HTML4::Sanitizer.safe_list_sanitizer.new)
    mattr_accessor(:allowed_tags)

      self.prefix_partial_path_with_controller_namespace = false
      sanitize_action_text_content(render_action_text_attachments(content))

    def sanitize_content_attachment(content_attachment)
      sanitizer.sanitize(
        content_attachment,
        tags: sanitizer_allowed_tags,
        attributes: sanitizer_allowed_attributes,
        scrubber: scrubber,
      )
    end

    def sanitize_action_text_content(content)
      sanitizer.sanitize(
        content.to_html,
        tags: sanitizer_allowed_tags,
        attributes: sanitizer_allowed_attributes,
        scrubber: scrubber,
      ).html_safe
    end

    def render_action_text_attachments(content)
      content.render_attachments do |attachment|
        unless attachment.in?(content.gallery_attachments)
          attachment.node.tap do |node|
            node.inner_html = render_action_text_attachment attachment, locals: { in_gallery: false }
          end
        end

        render(layout: attachment_gallery, object: attachment_gallery) do
          attachment_gallery.attachments.map do |attachment|
            attachment.node.inner_html = render_action_text_attachment attachment, locals: { in_gallery: true }
            attachment.to_html
          end.join.html_safe
        end.chomp
      end
    end

    def render_action_text_attachment(attachment, locals: {}) # :nodoc:
      options = { locals: locals, object: attachment, partial: attachment }

      if attachment.respond_to?(:to_attachable_partial_path)

######## 7-1-stable-actiontext.md * Update vendored trix version to 2.1.10 *John Hawthorn* * Avoid backtracing in plain_text_for_blockquote_node [CVE-2024-47888] *John Hawthorn* * Strip `content` attribute if the key is present but the value is empty *Jeremy Green* * Only sanitize `content` attribute when present in attachments. *Petrik de Heus* * Sanitize ActionText HTML ContentAttachment in Trix edit view [CVE-2024-32464] *Aaron Patterson* * Upgrade Trix to 2.1.1 to fix [CVE-2024-34341](https://github.com/basecamp/trix/security/advisories/GHSA-qjqp-xr96-cj99). *Rafael Mendonça França* * Compile ESM package that can be used directly in the browser as `actiontext.esm.js`. *Matias Grunberg* * Fix using actiontext.js with Sprockets. *Matias Grunberg* * Upgrade Trix to 2.0.7. *Hartley McGuire* * Fix using Trix with Sprockets. *Hartley McGuire* * Use `Rails::HTML5::SafeListSanitizer` by default in the Rails 7.1 configuration if it is supported. Action Text's sanitizer can be configured by setting `config.action_text.sanitizer_vendor`. Supported values are `Rails::HTML4::Sanitizer` or `Rails::HTML5::Sanitizer`. The Rails 7.1 configuration will set this to `Rails::HTML5::Sanitizer` when it is supported, and fall back to `Rails::HTML4::Sanitizer`. Previous configurations default to `Rails::HTML4::Sanitizer`. As a result of this change, the defaults for `ActionText::ContentHelper.allowed_tags` and `.allowed_attributes` are applied at runtime, so the value of these attributes is now 'nil' unless set by the application. You may call `sanitizer_allowed_tags` or `sanitizer_allowed_attributes` to inspect the tags and attributes being allowed by the sanitizer. *Mike Dalessio* * Attachables now can override default attachment missing template. When rendering Action Text attachments where the underlying attachable model has been removed, a fallback template is used. You now can override this template on a per-model basis. For example, you could render a placeholder image for a file attachment or the text "Deleted User" for a User attachment. *Matt Swanson*, *Joel Drapper* * Update bundled Trix version from `1.3.1` to `2.0.4`. *Sarah Ridge*, *Sean Doyle* * Apply `field_error_proc` to `rich_text_area` form fields. *Kaíque Kandy Koga* * Action Text attachment URLs rendered in a background job (a la Turbo Streams) now use `Rails.application.default_url_options` and `Rails.application.config.force_ssl` instead of `http://example.org`. *Jonathan Hefner* * Support `strict_loading:` option for `has_rich_text` declaration *Sean Doyle* * Update ContentAttachment so that it can encapsulate arbitrary HTML content in a document. *Jamis Buck* * Fix an issue that caused the content layout to render multiple times when a rich_text field was updated. *Jacob Herrington* Please check [7-0-stable](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-0-stable/actiontext/CHANGELOG.md) for previous changes. ######## 7-2-stable-actiontext.md * Update vendored trix version to 2.1.10 *John Hawthorn* * Avoid backtracing in plain_text_for_blockquote_node [CVE-2024-47888] *John Hawthorn* * Strip `content` attribute if the key is present but the value is empty *Jeremy Green* * Only sanitize `content` attribute when present in attachments. *Petrik de Heus* * Sanitize ActionText HTML ContentAttachment in Trix edit view [CVE-2024-32464] *Aaron Patterson*, *Zack Deveau* * Use `includes` instead of `eager_load` for `with_all_rich_text`. *Petrik de Heus* * Delegate `ActionText::Content#deconstruct` to `Nokogiri::XML::DocumentFragment#elements`. ```ruby content = ActionText::Content.new <<~HTML

Hello, world

The body
HTML content => [h1, div] assert_pattern { h1 => { content: "Hello, world" } } assert_pattern { div => { content: "The body" } } ``` *Sean Doyle* * Fix all Action Text database related models to respect `ActiveRecord::Base.table_name_prefix` configuration. *Chedli Bourguiba* * Compile ESM package that can be used directly in the browser as actiontext.esm.js *Matias Grunberg* * Fix using actiontext.js with Sprockets. *Matias Grunberg* * Upgrade Trix to 2.0.7 *Hartley McGuire* * Fix using Trix with Sprockets. *Hartley McGuire* Please check [7-1-stable](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/actiontext/CHANGELOG.md) for previous changes. ######## 8-0-stable-actiontext.md * Add rollup-plugin-terser as a dev dependency. *Édouard Chin* * Update vendored trix version to 2.1.10 *John Hawthorn* * Dispatch direct-upload events on attachment uploads When using Action Text's rich textarea, it's possible to attach files to the editor. Previously, that action didn't dispatch any events, which made it hard to react to the file uploads. For instance, if an upload failed, there was no way to notify the user about it, or remove the attachment from the editor. This commits adds new events - `direct-upload:start`, `direct-upload:progress`, and `direct-upload:end` - similar to how Active Storage's direct uploads work. *Matheus Richard*, *Brad Rees* * Add `store_if_blank` option to `has_rich_text` Pass `store_if_blank: false` to not create `ActionText::RichText` records when saving with a blank attribute, such as from an optional form parameter. ```ruby class Message has_rich_text :content, store_if_blank: false end Message.create(content: "hi") # creates an ActionText::RichText Message.create(content: "") # does not create an ActionText::RichText ``` *Alex Ghiculescu* * Strip `content` attribute if the key is present but the value is empty *Jeremy Green* * Rename `rich_text_area` methods into `rich_textarea` Old names are still available as aliases. *Sean Doyle* * Only sanitize `content` attribute when present in attachments. *Petrik de Heus* Please check [7-2-stable](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/actiontext/CHANGELOG.md) for previous changes. ######## 8-1-stable-actiontext.md * De-couple `@rails/actiontext/attachment_upload.js` from `Trix.Attachment` Implement `@rails/actiontext/index.js` with a `direct-upload:progress` event listeners and `Promise` resolution. *Sean Doyle* * Capture block content for form helper methods ```erb <%= rich_textarea_tag :content, nil do %>

hello world

<% end %> <%= rich_textarea :message, :content, input: "trix_input_1" do %>

hello world

<% end %> <%= form_with model: Message.new do |form| %> <%= form.rich_textarea :content do %>

hello world

<% end %> <% end %> ``` *Sean Doyle* * Generalize `:rich_text_area` Capybara selector Prepare for more Action Text-capable WYSIWYG editors by making `:rich_text_area` rely on the presence of `[role="textbox"]` and `[contenteditable]` HTML attributes rather than a `` element. *Sean Doyle* * Forward `fill_in_rich_text_area` options to Capybara ```ruby fill_in_rich_textarea "Rich text editor", id: "trix_editor_1", with: "Hello world!" ``` *Sean Doyle* * Attachment upload progress accounts for server processing time. *Jeremy Daer* * The Trix dependency is now satisfied by a gem, `action_text-trix`, rather than vendored files. This allows applications to bump Trix versions independently of Rails releases. Effectively this also upgrades Trix to `>= 2.1.15`. *Mike Dalessio* * Change `ActionText::RichText#embeds` assignment from `before_save` to `before_validation` *Sean Doyle* Please check [8-0-stable](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/8-0-stable/actiontext/CHANGELOG.md) for previous changes.

# frozen_string_literal: true

require "sidekiq/job"

module Sidekiq
  class Rails < ::Rails::Engine
    class Reloader
      def initialize(app = ::Rails.application)
        @app = app
      end

      def call
        @app.reloader.wrap do
          yield
        end
      end

      def inspect
        "#<Sidekiq::Rails::Reloader @app=#{@app.class.name}>"
      end
    end

    # By including the Options module, we allow AJs to directly control sidekiq features
    # via the *sidekiq_options* class method and, for instance, not use AJ's retry system.
    # AJ retries don't show up in the Sidekiq UI Retries tab, save any error data, can't be
    # manually retried, don't automatically die, etc.
    #
    #   class SomeJob < ActiveJob::Base
    #     queue_as :default
    #     sidekiq_options retry: 3, backtrace: 10
    #     def perform
    #     end
    #   end
    initializer "sidekiq.active_job_integration" do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        include ::Sidekiq::Job::Options unless respond_to?(:sidekiq_options)
      end
    end

    config.before_configuration do
      dep = ActiveSupport::Deprecation.new("7.0", "Sidekiq")
      dep.deprecate_methods(Sidekiq.singleton_class,
        default_worker_options: :default_job_options,
        "default_worker_options=": :default_job_options=)
    end

    # This hook happens after all initializers are run, just before returning
    # from config/environment.rb back to sidekiq/cli.rb.
    #
    # None of this matters on the client-side, only within the Sidekiq process itself.
    config.after_initialize do
      Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
        config[:reloader] = Sidekiq::Rails::Reloader.new

        # This is the integration code necessary so that if a job uses `Rails.logger.info "Hello"`,
        # it will appear in the Sidekiq console with all of the job context.
        unless ::Rails.logger == config.logger || ::ActiveSupport::Logger.logger_outputs_to?(::Rails.logger, $stdout)
          if ::Rails::VERSION::STRING < "7.1"
            ::Rails.logger.extend(::ActiveSupport::Logger.broadcast(config.logger))
          else
            ::Rails.logger.broadcast_to(config.logger)
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

require "set"

module Sidekiq
  class RedisClientAdapter
    BaseError = RedisClient::Error
    CommandError = RedisClient::CommandError

    # You can add/remove items or clear the whole thing if you don't want deprecation warnings.
    DEPRECATED_COMMANDS = %i[rpoplpush zrangebyscore zrevrange zrevrangebyscore getset hmset setex setnx].to_set

    module CompatMethods
      def info
        @client.call("INFO") { |i| i.lines(chomp: true).map { |l| l.split(":", 2) }.select { |l| l.size == 2 }.to_h }
      end

      def evalsha(sha, keys, argv)
        @client.call("EVALSHA", sha, keys.size, *keys, *argv)
      end

      # this is the set of Redis commands used by Sidekiq. Not guaranteed
      # to be comprehensive, we use this as a performance enhancement to
      # avoid calling method_missing on most commands
      USED_COMMANDS = %w[bitfield bitfield_ro del exists expire flushdb
        get hdel hget hgetall hincrby hlen hmget hset hsetnx incr incrby
        lindex llen lmove lpop lpush lrange lrem mget mset ping pttl
        publish rpop rpush sadd scard script set sismember smembers
        srem ttl type unlink zadd zcard zincrby zrange zrem
        zremrangebyrank zremrangebyscore]

      USED_COMMANDS.each do |name|
        define_method(name) do |*args, **kwargs|
          @client.call(name, *args, **kwargs)
        end
      end

      private

      # this allows us to use methods like `conn.hmset(...)` instead of having to use
      # redis-client's native `conn.call("hmset", ...)`
      def method_missing(*args, &block)
        warn("[sidekiq#5788] Redis has deprecated the `#{args.first}`command, called at #{caller(1..1)}") if DEPRECATED_COMMANDS.include?(args.first)
        @client.call(*args, *block)
      end
      ruby2_keywords :method_missing if respond_to?(:ruby2_keywords, true)

      def respond_to_missing?(name, include_private = false)
        super # Appease the linter. We can't tell what is a valid command.
      end
    end

    CompatClient = RedisClient::Decorator.create(CompatMethods)

content.text:
# Rails 7.0.8.7 to 8.1.0: changes that affect Margin Notes

I compared the unpacked 7.0.8.7 and 8.1.0 gems for every Rails component, read the 7.1, 7.2, 8.0 and 8.1 changelogs, and read Sidekiq 6.5.12 and 7.3.9. Nothing in the app was installed, changed or run. Each claim is tagged **[changelog]**, **[code]** (gem or app source I read) or **[inference]**.

The changes most likely to slip through are the four that change data or delivered results without raising an error:
- **Import#apply** now commits a half-finished import.
- **Digest emails** now cover the reader's local day instead of the UTC day.
- **Digest jobs** queued by new web servers fail on old workers during a rolling deploy.
- **Import receipt CSVs** come out with an empty DOI column.

There are also about ten mechanical breakages that booting the app or running its tests would catch.

## Facts about the app that the ratings depend on (please correct any that are wrong)

- **Database:** PostgreSQL only (`config/database.yml:18`). `config.time_zone` is not set, so the app runs in UTC. Each reader's time zone is stored in `users.time_zone`.
- **Framework defaults:** `config.load_defaults 7.0` (`config/application.rb:12`). Rails 8.1 still accepts it **[code]**. I assumed you keep it for the upgrade.
- **Jobs:**
  - Active Job runs on the **built-in Rails Sidekiq adapter** with Sidekiq 6.5.12 and redis 4.8.1 (`config/application.rb:24`). Tests use the `:test` adapter.
  - `ExportJob` is a native Sidekiq job.
  - `NoteReminderJob` is scheduled days ahead, so jobs queued under 7.0 will run under 8.1.
  - **I assumed web servers and Sidekiq workers are deployed separately**, so old and new versions can overlap.
- **Sidekiq and Rack versions:** the upgrade can keep Sidekiq 6.5.12, because Rails 8.1 still ships its adapter (removal is planned for 8.2) **[code]**. Sidekiq 6.5.12 requires `rack ~> 2.0`, so Rack should stay at 2.2.x **[inference]**. Sidekiq 6.5.12's Rails integration already supports the 7.1+ logger **[code]**.
- **Front end:** a server-rendered HTML app using Sprockets, importmap and Turbo. No JSON responses.
- **Action Text:** the app loads its own copy of Trix 1.3.5 (`app/views/layouts/application.html.erb:13`). The allowlist is extended in `config/initializers/action_text.rb:3`.
- **Active Storage:** Disk service only, no image processing.
- **Cache:** production doesn't set a cache store, so it uses the default file store. The only fragment cache is in `app/views/exports/_export.html.erb:26`.
- **Provider settings:** the citation provider is configured through `Rails.application.secrets` and `config/secrets.yml`.
- **Runtime versions:** Ruby 3.3.6 meets 8.1's `>= 3.2` requirement. All other locked gem versions satisfy 8.1's dependency ranges **[code]**.

## High risk

**1. A `return` inside a transaction now commits instead of rolling back**
- **Before:** in 7.0, leaving a `transaction` block early with `return` rolled the transaction back **[code]**.
- **Now:** 8.0 removed the option to keep that, and 8.1 commits **[code, changelog]**.
- **Where:** `app/models/import.rb:53-56` returns `false` from inside `transaction do` when a row fails to save.
- **What could go wrong:** the Import record and the rows saved before the failing row stay in the database, while the user is told nothing was saved. `test/controllers/imports_controller_test.rb:65-72` should catch it.
- **Link:** https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/48600

**2. Time arguments to jobs now keep the reader's time zone**
- **Before:** `ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone` job arguments came back in the worker's zone (UTC) **[code]**.
- **Now:** since 7.1 they come back in the zone they were sent from **[code, changelog]**.
- **Where:** `app/models/user.rb:41` passes the reader's local `requested_at`. `app/mailers/digest_mailer.rb:8-9` uses `.to_date` and `.all_day` on it.
- **What could go wrong:**
  - The digest covers the reader's local day, and the subject date changes (for example October 04 instead of October 05 in `test/controllers/digests_controller_test.rb:33`).
  - The once-per-day limit is still counted per UTC day.
  - The comments in the mailer and the hint in `app/views/accounts/edit.html.erb:16` will no longer be true.
- **Link:** https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md (7.1.3)

**3. BigDecimal job arguments now use a format 7.0 workers can't read**
- **Before:** 7.0 queued a BigDecimal as a plain string.
- **Now:** 8.1 always wraps it as `ActiveJob::Serializers::BigDecimalSerializer`. The opt-out setting was removed in 8.0 **[code, changelog]**.
- **Where:** `app/models/user.rb:41` passes `reading_completion`, a BigDecimal (`user.rb:56`).
- **What could go wrong:** during a rolling deploy, a 7.0 worker raises "Serializer ... is not known", which becomes `DeserializationError`. `DigestJob` doesn't discard on that, so Sidekiq retries it until a new worker picks it up. Digests are delayed, and could be lost if retries run out. The reverse direction is fine: `BigDecimal(params[:completion])` at `digest_mailer.rb:10` accepts the old string **[code]**.
- **Link:** https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md

**4. `record[:id]` no longer returns a custom primary key**
- **Before:** in 7.0, `read_attribute(:id)` mapped to the primary key.
- **Now:** in 7.2+, it reads a column literally named `id`. `citations` has no such column, so the value is `nil` with no error **[code]**.
- **Where:** `app/models/import.rb:68` (`citation[:id]`).
- **What could go wrong:** the DOI column of the import receipt CSV is silently empty. `test/controllers/imports_controller_test.rb:45` should catch it. The fix is `citation.doi` or `citation.id`.
- **Link:** https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md

**5. `TimeWithZone#to_time` now keeps the full zone, not just the offset**
- **Before:** under your defaults, `to_time` returned a Time with a fixed offset.
- **Now:** 8.1 always returns a Time carrying the zone **[code, changelog]**.
- **Where:** `app/models/note.rb:44` (`next_day_reminder_at`), shown in `app/views/notes/_reminder.html.erb:19`.
- **What could go wrong:** across a daylight saving change, the "24 hours later" preview shows the new offset and wall-clock time, for example 08:00 at UTC-05:00 instead of 09:00 at UTC-04:00. The scheduled time itself is unchanged, so this only affects the label **[inference]**. `test/controllers/reminders_controller_test.rb:21` and the comment at `note.rb:40-42` will disagree.
- **Link:** https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/8-1-stable/activesupport/CHANGELOG.md (8.1.0)

**6. A negative cache `expires_in` now means the entry never expires**
- **Before:** in 7.0, a negative value made the entry expire immediately.
- **Now:** since 7.1 the option is dropped and an error is logged and reported. Under your defaults it doesn't raise **[code, changelog]**.
- **Where:** `app/views/exports/_export.html.erb:26`, where `expires_at - Time.current` is negative for expired exports.
- **What could go wrong:** the "Expired" fragment is cached with no expiry, and every render logs an `ArgumentError`. What users see stays correct, so the impact is small **[inference]**.
- **Link:** https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/activesupport/CHANGELOG.md

**7. Action Text's plain-text conversion changed**
- **Before:** `<script>` and `<style>` text was included, and numbered-list bullets counted whitespace nodes.
- **Now:** `<script>` and `<style>` produce no text, and numbering counts only elements **[code]**.
- **Where:** `app/models/export.rb:110` builds the Markdown export from `to_plain_text`, and imported `body_html` is stored as given. Excerpts in `app/views/notes/index.html.erb:53` are also affected.
- **What could go wrong:** export file contents change for those notes. This is a narrow change.
- **Link:** none. I found no changelog entry for this; it comes from diffing `plain_text_conversion.rb`.

**8. The "Astana" time zone now maps to Asia/Almaty**
- **Before:** Asia/Dhaka (UTC+6).
- **Now:** Asia/Almaty, which is UTC+5 with current tz data **[code, changelog]**.
- **Where:** `app/models/user.rb:13` and `:22`, and `note.rb:37`.
- **What could go wrong:** for readers set to Astana, reminder times shift by an hour, both when entered and when displayed. Other mapping changes (Canberra, Greenland, the new Asuncion zone) don't change offsets **[inference]**.
- **Link:** https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activesupport/CHANGELOG.md

## Medium risk

**`Rails.application.secrets` was removed**
- **Before:** deprecated in 7.1. **Now:** removed in 7.2 **[changelog]**.
- **Where:** `app/models/citation/provider.rb:13`, `config/secrets.yml`, and the test helper at `test/controllers/citation_enrichments_controller_test.rb:45,117-122`.
- **What could go wrong:** a `NoMethodError` when enrichment runs, not at boot.
- **Decision needed:** there's no direct replacement. Choose between `config_for(:citation_provider)`, credentials, or ENV. Keep the `.to_json` quoting that the environment test checks.
- **Link:** https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/railties/CHANGELOG.md

**The built-in Sidekiq adapter is deprecated and will be removed in 8.2**
- 8.1 logs a deprecation warning when the adapter is set at `config/application.rb:24` **[code, changelog]**.
- The fix is Sidekiq 7.3.3 or later. In Sidekiq 7.3.9's source **[code]**:
  - `redis.sadd` returns 0 or 1. Both are truthy in Ruby, so the once-per-day digest check at `app/models/user.rb:38` silently stops working.
  - Redis errors become `RedisClient::Error`, so `rescue Redis::BaseError` at `app/models/notebook.rb:28` stops catching them.
  - Strict argument checking raises on the symbol-key hash `{ format: "markdown" }` at `notebook.rb:26`.
- The wrapper class name is unchanged, so queued jobs stay compatible **[code]**.
- **Link:** https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/8-1-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md

**`show_exceptions = false` in the test environment is no longer supported**
- **Where:** `config/environments/test.rb:31`.
- **What changed:** 7.2 removed support for `true` and `false`. 8.1 treats any unrecognised value as `:all`, so test exceptions are rendered as error pages instead of raised, with no warning **[code, changelog]**.
- **What could go wrong:** the many `assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound)` tests will fail.
- **Decision needed:** `:none` keeps today's behaviour; `:rescuable` is the new generated default.

**Framework defaults after 7.0 (only matters when you raise `load_defaults`)**

Each new default breaks something specific in this app **[code]**:
- **7.1, `default_column_serializer = nil`:** `serialize :preferences` at `app/models/notebook.rb:7` raises.
- **7.1, `raise_on_assign_to_attr_readonly`:** the notebook settings form re-submits the slug (`app/controllers/notebooks_controller.rb:40`), which then raises.
- **7.1, `raise_on_invalid_cache_expiration_time`:** expired exports make the exports page raise (see High item 6).
- **7.1, `action_text.sanitizer_vendor`:** switches Action Text to the HTML5 sanitizer.
- **7.2, `postgresql_adapter_decode_dates`:** `Date.iso8601(day)` at `notebook.rb:40` gets a `Date` instead of a string and raises a `TypeError`.
- **8.0, `strict_freshness`:** changes how ETags and `If-Modified-Since` interact in `app/controllers/export_downloads_controller.rb:11`.

## Low risk (booting or running the tests would catch these)

- **`serialize :tags, JSON`** (`note.rb:12`): the positional coder argument now raises; use `coder: JSON` **[code]**.
- **`enum status: {...}, _prefix: true`** (`note.rb:10`): the keyword form now raises an `ArgumentError`; use `enum :status, {...}, prefix: true` **[code]**.
- **`alias_attribute :highlight_color, :color`** (`note.rb:14`): `color` is a store accessor, not an attribute, so this raises since 7.2; define the reader and writer with `alias_method` **[code]**.
- **`fragments.sum`** (`export.rb:42`): Rails no longer sums strings (7.1), so this raises a `TypeError` and exports never finish; use `join` **[code]**.
- **`set(wait_until: reminder_epoch)` with an Integer** (`note.rb:61`): raises `NoMethodError` (`utc`) when the job is queued (7.2); use `Time.at(reminder_epoch)` **[code]**.
- **`wait: :exponentially_longer`** (`app/jobs/citation_enrichment_job.rb:7`): removed in 7.2, and it only raises when a retry happens. If missed in production, citations stay "pending" for good. Use `:polynomially_longer`, which has the same timing **[code]**.
- **`get "/notes", "/journal", ...`** (`config/routes.rb:18`): multiple paths in one route were removed in 8.1 and now raise when the routes load; write two routes and keep the `journal` name **[code, changelog]**.
- **`allowed_tags +=`** (`config/initializers/action_text.rb:3`): `allowed_tags` is now `nil` by default (7.1), so boot fails. Build the list from `sanitizer.class.allowed_tags` plus `action-text-attachment`, `figure`, `figcaption`, `details` and `summary`. Setting only `%w[details summary]` would silently strip every other tag **[code]**.
- **Trix:** Action Text 8.1 depends on the `action_text-trix` gem (Trix 2.1.15), but the app keeps loading its own 1.3.5. `actiontext.js` still uses the same Trix API, so this probably works, but check uploads in a browser **[inference]**.
- **Schema dump and dev secret:** `db/schema.rb` will be rewritten with an 8.1 header, and the development secret moves to `tmp/local_secret.txt`, which signs out local sessions **[inference]**.

## Judged not relevant

- **MySQL, SQLite and Trilogy changes:** the app uses PostgreSQL.
- **PostgreSQL minimum version:** still 9.3; `pg 1.6.0` meets `~> 1.1`.
- **Jobs enqueued inside a transaction:** 8.1 defaults to queuing immediately, as 7.0 did, so the jobs queued under `with_lock` behave as before **[code]**.
- **Rack 3 changes** (such as `:unprocessable_entity`): Rack isn't upgraded.
- **Action Cable** (no channels), **Action Mailbox** (unused), **Active Storage** variants, previews and cloud services (Disk only, no image processing).
- **JSON escaping and `escape_json_responses`:** the app serves HTML only; Jbuilder is installed but has no templates.
- **Solid Queue, Propshaft and YJIT:** these are new-app generator defaults only.
- **Fixes released after 8.1.0** (8.1.1 to 8.1.4, such as the Kyiv zone rename and integer-string limits): not part of 8.1.0.
- **Unchanged:** `TimeZone#iso8601`, `TimeZone#at`, the default locales (only additions), and `select_rows` on a relation.

The unpacked gems and changelogs are in `/tmp/gems/old`, `/tmp/gems/new`, `/tmp/gems/cl`, `/tmp/gems/sidekiq` and `/tmp/gems/sidekiq7`, if you want to look closer.
